newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS - SFE wheat drifts after ABARE crop estimate.
newsitem.headline: RTRS - SFE wheat drifts after ABARE crop estimate.

text.p: Australian wheat futures drifted sideways in dull trading on Wednesday after Chicago's overnight fall.
Tuesday's active market slowed on Wednesday, with only two trades in January 1997 struck on the Sydney Futures Exchange. The contract edged up by 50 cents to A$153.00 a tonne on the trade.
Ben Suttie of C,A & L Bell Commodities Corp Pty Ltd described Tuesday's ABARE forecast of an Australian 1996/97 wheat crop of 20.9 million tonnes as "fairly bearish as we go into harvest".
In a disappointing market Bell unsuccessfully tried to buy January 1997 at A$150.00, Suttie said.
But Chicago wheat's slight rally toward last night's close might cause a short-term market bounce, Suttie said.
"You might just see in the next couple of days days a bit of support and short covering and then maybe they'll sell it again," he said.
